Subject: Regional failover scope & DPA addendum questions

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the demo last week — we’re close on product fit, but our legal and infra teams have a few open items before procurement can sign the SOW/DPA. Two quick clarifying questions on region pinning and transient failover: 

1) Can Redwood commit that customer data will be processed only in the pinned region (EU) except for operational failover? If failover occurs, what is the maximum allowable transient processing window before data is removed from the failover region?

2) For transient failover paths (e.g., US fallback for EU region), what subprocessors might receive replicated telemetry/metrics or cached KV data? We need a roster and approximate replication TTLs to satisfy our security review.

Also, please confirm whether KMS keys for EU-pinned customers will be provisioned in an EU keyring that prevents key-use outside the region. If not, we need language for the DPA addendum that documents the limitation.

Can we get a short written summary we can attach to our procurement checklist by COB Tuesday?

—Sarah
Sarah Liu

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Marcus (infra) and Grace (legal) so we can give a single doc you can attach to procurement. High level answers now, full details and a DPA addendum draft attached: network-failover-sketch.png; DPA-addendum-ACME-draft.pdf.

- Region affinity: Redwood can provide region affinity (pinning) for customer workloads and data. Affinity means primary processing and persistent stores remain in the pinned region for normal operations.

- Transient failover window: We operate with a design target of transient failover under 24 hours for customer request routing; engineering may retain replicated ephemeral KV/cache artifacts up to 72 hours in exceptional, extended failover scenarios (disaster recovery, long network partitions). We will call this out as a conditional operational carveout in the DPA addendum.

- Subprocessors & telemetry: We will provide a roster of subprocessors by region; attached is an initial APAC/EU/US roster (regional-subprocessor-roster.csv). Telemetry and metrics are aggregated and sent to our telemetry pipeline; but in transient failover cases, aggregates may be routed through the failover region. We will include explicit limits on what telemetry contains and retention windows.

- KMS: For EU-pinned customers we support customer-managed keys (CMK) in EU keyrings for Dedicated/Private customers. For Hosted (standard) customers, we offer Redwood-managed EU KMS keys—these keys are logically bound to EU keyrings, but there are operational exceptions for emergency ops (we document this in the addendum). If strict key residency is required, we recommend Dedicated or Private deployment.

I’ll follow up with the engineering confirmations on TTLs and the precise subprocessor list. Are you available for a 30-minute redline session on Tue 2026-08-31 at 10am PT?

Thanks,
Irene

Irene / Grace — technical answers below (summary for customer doc):

- Transient failover behavior:
  * Normal: requests routed to pinned region; no cross-region persistent replication.
  * Failover (operational): requests can be served from a failover region; ephemeral KV/cache items are replicated on demand. Engineering default target to restore pinning is 24 hours.
  * Maximum retention: We do not persist customer user data in the failover region beyond 72 hours unless there is a documented incident requiring extended recovery. We will expressly exclude automatic cross-region synchronous persistence for persistent DBs.

- KV/cache specifics:
  * Per-customer KV TTL default during failover: 24h.
  * Background retention: background reconciliation jobs may hold tombstones/metadata for up to 72h to avoid re-sync storms.

- Telemetry & subprocessors:
  * Aggregated telemetry (non-PII) may traverse our global telemetry pipeline; during failover those aggregates could be processed in the failover region.
  * Subprocessors that may see failover telemetry: Datadog EU/US (metrics), S3 buckets operated by our cloud provider in failover region, and a small set of ops tooling vendors (PagerDuty, Rollbar) — full list in regional-subprocessor-roster.csv.

- KMS note:
  * Hosted customers: Redwood-managed keys provisioned in region-bound keyrings; key use is restricted via IAM policies but emergency operations may involve cross-region key-use by a scoped ops runbook.
  * Dedicated/Private: support customer-managed key material in customer AWS/GCP keyrings.

Irene — I attached network-failover-sketch.png and the updated regional-subprocessor-roster.csv for Acme. If Grace wants different legal framing for the 72h maximum, flag it and I’ll update the doc.

—Marcus

Hi Sarah / Tom — following up with the agreed summary (please see attached DPA-addendum-ACME-draft.pdf and regional-subprocessor-roster.csv). Key commitments we can make in the DPA addendum: 

1) Region affinity: Primary processing and persistent storage will remain in the pinned region (EU) for normal operations.

2) Transient failover: Redwood’s operational target to return to pinned-region processing is 24 hours. Exceptional failovers may result in transient processing in a failover region for up to 72 hours; such events will be logged, and customers will be notified. We will include an operationally-scoped incident carveout in the addendum.

3) Subprocessor visibility: We included a per-region roster showing services that might receive aggregated telemetry or temporary artifacts during failover. We commit to giving you 30 days' notice for material subprocessor changes.

4) KMS options: For strict key residency we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments with customer-managed key material. For Hosted customers, Redwood-managed EU keyrings are used and emergency ops are documented as exceptions in the addendum.

Next steps: 
- If this aligns, can Grace and I join your procurement redline session Tue 2026-08-31 10:00 PT (you proposed) to walk the addendum?
- If Acme needs shorter maximum windows than 72 hours, let us know and we can evaluate product/ops changes but that may require Dedicated/Private commitments.

Thanks — happy to tighten language in real-time during the call.

Best,
